summary: This document defines a WebSocket subprotocol that lets Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) devices exchange messages reliably over a WebSocket connection. That makes SIP usable in web-oriented deployments, such as in browsers.

eli5.summary: Phone-call software normally talks over its own special lines. This lets it talk through the same open doorway that websites use, so a web page can make calls.

questions: how to use sip in a web browser
how to use sip over websocket

subtitle: How SIP messages ride over a WebSocket connection, so browsers and other web clients can use SIP.

tldr.problem: SIP needs a transport, but some environments, such as web browsers, do not let SIP elements use UDP or TCP directly. They do offer WebSocket.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a WebSocket subprotocol named sip. SIP messages travel one per WebSocket message over a reliable transport, with new transport values WS and WSS, a URI parameter ws and new NAPTR service values.
tldr.outcome: SIP can be used in web-oriented deployments. Media transport is out of scope, and the RFC recommends secure WebSocket (TLS) for the SIP traffic.

today: RFC 7118 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2014. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why SIP Over WebSocket
sections.content:
The WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455) lets clients and servers exchange messages over a persistent TCP connection, optionally secured with TLS. Its opening handshake uses HTTP semantics, so it can reuse existing HTTP infrastructure. Modern web browsers include a WebSocket client stack, and the RFC expects other client applications to follow.

This document defines a WebSocket subprotocol for carrying SIP messages between a WebSocket client and server. It also defines a reliable, message-boundary-preserving transport for SIP, and DNS NAPTR service values and procedures for SIP entities using it. Media transport is out of scope.

The RFC also relaxes one requirement of RFC 3261: the rule that a SIP server transport must add a received parameter to the top Via header in certain circumstances.
sections.eli5: Web pages can already open a long-lasting line to a server. This document shows how phone-call messages can use that same line.

sections.title: The WebSocket Protocol in Brief
sections.content:
WebSocket is a transport layer on top of TCP (optionally TLS) in which client and server exchange message units in both directions. It defines a connection handshake, subprotocol and extension negotiation, a frame format, a masking mechanism and status codes for disconnection causes.

The handshake is an HTTP GET with an Upgrade request. The server answers with HTTP status 101 if negotiation succeeded, and the connection then upgrades from HTTP to WebSocket. During the handshake the two sides agree on the application protocol to run on top, called a WebSocket subprotocol. Unlike plain HTTP, the connection is persistent.

Message units carry either UTF-8 text or binary data and may be split over several frames. Because message boundaries are preserved, this is a message-boundary-preserving transport.
sections.eli5: WebSocket is a phone line that stays open after the first hello. Both sides can talk whenever they like, and each sentence arrives as one whole piece.

sections.title: The Handshake
sections.content:
The client and server negotiate the WebSocket SIP subprotocol during the normal WebSocket handshake. The client MUST include the value sip in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header of its request, and the server's 101 reply MUST contain sip in the same header.

The client opens a WebSocket connection when it needs to send a SIP request and no connection exists yet. If no HTTP 101 response arrives, this counts as a transaction error under RFC 3261, Section 8.1.3.1. After negotiation the connection carries SIP requests and responses, and messages other than SIP requests and responses MUST NOT be sent on it.

The RFC's registration example shows the flow: a browser-based client opens a secure WebSocket connection to a SIP proxy/registrar, then sends a REGISTER and receives a 200 OK.
sections.eli5: The two sides say "let's speak SIP" when the line opens. After that, only phone-call messages are allowed on it.

sections.title: How SIP Messages Are Encoded
sections.content:
WebSocket messages travel in UTF-8 text frames or binary frames. SIP allows both text and binary bodies, so clients and servers MUST accept both kinds of frame. If even one non-UTF-8 symbol appears anywhere in the SIP message, headers or body, the whole message MUST be sent in a binary WebSocket message.

Because of how JavaScript and the WebSocket API work, the RFC RECOMMENDS UTF-8 (or ASCII, a subset of it) for SIP messages carried this way.
sections.eli5: Messages can go in a text envelope or a mystery-box envelope. If anything odd is inside, use the mystery box for the whole message.

sections.title: The SIP WebSocket Transport
sections.content:
WebSocket is reliable, so the SIP WebSocket transport is a reliable SIP transport. Client and server transactions MUST follow the RFC 3261 procedures and timer values for reliable transports.

Each SIP message MUST be carried in a single WebSocket message, and a WebSocket message MUST NOT contain more than one SIP message. Since message boundaries are preserved, the Content-Length header is not necessary, which simplifies parsing.

The Via header transport value is WS for plain WebSocket and WSS for secure WebSocket. A SIP URI uses the transport parameter value ws.

RFC 3261 says a server MUST add a received parameter to the top Via header in some cases. With HTTP proxies or TCP load balancers in front of the server, that could reveal internal network topology, and responses can only go back on the existing connection anyway. So a SIP WebSocket Server MAY choose not to add it, and clients MUST accept responses without it. A WebSocket-only client is not required to implement UDP and TCP.

To keep connections open, either side may send WebSocket Ping frames. Browsers do not let applications control this, and the CRLF keep-alive mechanisms from RFC 5626 and RFC 6223 also work.
sections.eli5: One WebSocket message holds exactly one SIP message, so nobody has to count how long each one is. The line is trusted to deliver everything, so no extra delivery checks are needed.

sections.title: Finding a SIP WebSocket Server
sections.content:
RFC 3263 describes how SIP entities locate servers. This RFC defines the NAPTR service value SIP+D2W for servers supporting plain WebSocket and SIPS+D2W for servers supporting secure WebSocket.

The RFC notes that when it was written, commonly available WebSocket client stacks in JavaScript engines and browsers could not perform DNS NAPTR or SRV queries. Without SRV records or an explicit port, the default port is 80 for a sip URI with the ws transport parameter and 443 for a sips URI with it.
sections.eli5: This is the address book entry that tells a client where to knock. If no door number is given, it uses 80 for ordinary and 443 for the locked one.

sections.title: Authentication
sections.content:
WebSocket defines no authentication mechanism of its own; servers can use any mechanism available to a generic HTTP server during the handshake, such as cookies, HTTP authentication or TLS authentication. To get interoperability, the RFC sets these rules:

  • A client MUST be ready to add a session cookie if it runs in a browser and previously got one from the web server whose domain matches the WebSocket URI.
  • A client MUST be ready to be challenged with an HTTP 401 during the handshake.
  • A client MAY use TLS client authentication on a secure connection. That is governed by HTTP rules rather than SIP rules.
  • A server MUST be ready to read session cookies in the handshake request.
  • A server SHOULD be able to reject a handshake with a 401 and a Basic/Digest challenge.

Whether or not the handshake requires authentication, authentication MAY also be requested at the SIP level. Appendix A describes three use cases: SIP authentication only, web authentication only (a session token passed as a URL query parameter), and cookie-based authentication.
sections.eli5: You can show your ID at the front gate (the web login), at the phone desk (SIP), or both. The rules say what each side must be ready for.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
It is RECOMMENDED that SIP traffic over WebSocket be protected with a secure WebSocket connection, which is TLS over TCP. With SIP over secure WebSocket, the client MUST authenticate the server's certificate according to the validation procedure in RFC 6455. This differs from the SIP domain certificate procedure in RFC 5922, so certificates suited to SIP over TLS over TCP will probably not suit secure WebSocket.

The sips scheme requires the entire request path to be secure; if that path includes a WebSocket connection, it MUST be a secure one.

IANA registered the sip subprotocol in the WebSocket Subprotocol Name registry and the NAPTR values SIP+D2W and SIPS+D2W. It also added references to existing SIP registries and created a new SIP Transport subregistry listing UDP, TCP, TLS, SCTP, TLS-SCTP, WS and WSS, with registration by Standards Action.
sections.eli5: Use the locked version of the line so nobody can listen in, and make sure the lock really belongs to the right house.
